rule: Every operation in schemas/tauri-bridge-v1/bridge.schema.json must be listed under exactly one service in schemas/service-contracts-v1/registry.json, which states this rule about itself under operation_rules.ownership: "Each operation has exactly one owner service." An operation that belongs to no service cannot be named as a recovery action, because recovery actions resolve against that registry. The contract gate fails when a real unowned operation is absent from this list, and fails when a listed entry has since been given an owner. An entry is a justification, not an exemption: it records why the operation has no service yet, and it is removed as soon as one takes it. This file is gate configuration, not a contract surface, which is why it lives under tools/ rather than schemas/.

unowned.reason: The operation is declared by bridge.schema.json and is already given the owner RequirementService by both workspace.manifest.json and payloads.json, but that owner is the subject of an unlocked proposal rather than a locked decision: docs/ROADMAP.md, under "Trace-link operation ownership (open decision, not locked)", records the candidate owners and their trade-offs and recommends RequirementService, and docs/TRACEABILITY.md points at that block. Listing the operation under a service in the registry would settle that proposal by editing a contract, which is precisely what the proposal says must not happen before a human decides; the registry is the one of the four places that carries no value to align with yet. Nothing else is missing either way: the operation is declared with no handler, so no caller can reach it.
